what_it_does: FPGAs (field-programmable gate arrays) are chips whose internal wiring can be reconfigured — essentially blank chips that designers program to behave like custom circuits. Designers exploring FPGA architectures have traditionally been limited to flat, two-dimensional chip layouts. FPGen-3D is an automated framework that generates three-dimensional FPGA designs — chips stacked in layers connected by vertical wires — from a simple set of user-specified parameters, without requiring manual design work for each variant. It produces complete chip blueprints (called RTL, register-transfer level descriptions — essentially a precise textual recipe that a factory can use to manufacture the chip) as well as routing results and the programming files (bitstreams) needed to configure the chip. The tool explores different ways to run vertical connections through 3D switch blocks (the routing crossroads inside an FPGA) and 3D logic blocks (the units that do computation), letting researchers quickly compare many architectural options that would previously have taken months to evaluate by hand.
